name: Peshawar city
why: Picked from the real stack: a cluster of cells near the city centre bright in HH on every date, with a small seasonal spread. It lies at the edge of the 2 July HV interference, so that date also shows the interference on a target that otherwise does not move.

name: Built-up area near Hazro
role: Stable urban control, outside the 2 July interference
why: A stable bright cluster far from the western area, so its HV is usable on all dates. A second control for the first. A cluster west of Mardan was tried first and rejected: on all nine dates its HH spread was 2.1 dB, because of one high reading on 6 October.

name: Tarbela Reservoir, main pool
why: The dark stable cluster in the main pool, well inside the shoreline at every reservoir level seen this season.

name: Tarbela Reservoir, south-east shore
why: Red in the seasonal composite: much brighter in July and October than in August. The strongest seasonal change in the window, with a dated independent reference in the published reservoir level.

name: Plain west-north-west of Swabi
role: Plain area, rises in August and falls part way by October
why: Among the strongest seasonal HH and HV spreads on the plain, in a block of cells that moved together.

name: Plain east of Mardan
role: Plain area, rises from July to late September
why: One of the largest blocks that was dark in July and stayed brighter through October, unlike the Swabi site, which falls more.

name: Indus River near Attock
why: Dark through the monsoon and much brighter in late September and October. The river stretch with the clearest seasonal change.
